concepts.title: Terms of joint dynamics
concepts.description: The matrix multiplies joint acceleration; V groups centrifugal/Coriolis terms and G represents gravity.

concepts.title: Dimensions of joint dynamics
concepts.description: The n×n inertia matrix maps n joint accelerations to n joint efforts, so V must also have n entries.

concepts.title: First-order state representation
concepts.description: Position and velocity together determine the instantaneous state; acceleration is obtained from the dynamics and input.

concepts.title: Configuration dependence is not universal entrywise
concepts.description: The example directly shows that configuration dependence is a property of the matrix function, not a requirement that every entry vary with every coordinate.
concepts.subtopic: Configuration dependence is not universal entrywise

concepts.title: Reading the two-link mass model
concepts.description: The diagram places m1 at the first link’s distal end and m2 at the second link’s distal end.

concepts.title: Positive-definite inertia and energy
concepts.description: The kinetic energy ½zᵀMz is positive for nonzero generalized velocity under these assumptions; this implies invertibility, not an identity matrix.

concepts.title: Inertia need not fail at kinematic singularity
concepts.description: At θ2=0, det M=l1²l2²m1m2>0, while det J=l1l2sinθ2=0.
concepts.subtopic: Inertia need not fail at kinematic singularity

concepts.title: Squared and mixed rates
concepts.description: The slide labels the squared-rate terms centrifugal and the mixed-rate terms Coriolis in this coordinate expansion.

concepts.title: Evaluate the joint velocity term
concepts.description: With h=m2l1l2sinθ2=6, V1=−h(qdot2²+2qdot1qdot2)=−6(4+4)=−48 and V2=h qdot1²=6.

concepts.title: Gravity at rest
concepts.description: The inertia and velocity terms vanish at rest, leaving the torque needed to balance gravity.

concepts.title: Evaluate gravity torques
concepts.description: cos(θ1+θ2)=0 removes the distal-link moment term; (m1+m2)l1gcosθ1=50 remains in G1.

concepts.title: Dimensions of separated velocity coefficients
concepts.description: There are4·3/2=6 distinct unordered mixed-rate products and four squared rates.

concepts.title: Complete mixed-rate vector
concepts.description: Three joints have three unordered pairs:12,13 and23; adjacent pairs alone are incomplete and reversed duplicates are not new pairs.

concepts.title: Two-link separated matrices
concepts.description: Multiplying B by qdot1qdot2 gives the mixed first component; multiplying C by[qdot1²,qdot2²]ᵀ gives the two squared terms.

concepts.title: Two meanings of C
concepts.description: The local notation defines a configuration-only matrix of squared-rate coefficients; another convention uses a velocity-dependent matrix multiplying first-power rates.

concepts.title: Task-space effort and acceleration
concepts.description: The generalized force or wrench must be power-conjugate to the selected task velocity; a geometric angular velocity and an arbitrary orientation-parameter derivative are not interchangeable.

concepts.title: Why torque uses the transpose
concepts.description: Fᵀv=FᵀJqdot=(JᵀF)ᵀqdot, so matching coefficients of qdot gives τ=JᵀF.

concepts.title: When the inverse-transpose step exists
concepts.description: An ordinary inverse transpose exists only for a square nonsingular matrix; the transpose mapping itself does not require that condition.

concepts.title: A common frame is required
concepts.description: The matrix-vector components must describe compatible coordinate bases and, for a full wrench, compatible reference points.

concepts.title: Product rule for task acceleration
concepts.description: Differentiate both factors of J(q)qdot; J changes with configuration, producing Jdot qdot.

concepts.title: Solve for joint acceleration
concepts.description: Subtract the velocity term to get(4,6), then apply J⁻¹=diag(1/2,1), yielding(2,6).

concepts.title: Transformed inertia order
concepts.description: Substitute qddot=J⁻¹(xddot−Jdot qdot) into F=J⁻ᵀτ; the xddot coefficient is J⁻ᵀMJ⁻¹.

concepts.title: Transformed velocity term
concepts.description: Solving the acceleration mapping subtracts J⁻¹Jdot qdot before multiplication by M and J⁻ᵀ.

concepts.title: Positive inertia under coordinate change
concepts.description: The congruence transformation preserves the positive quadratic form; J⁻¹y is nonzero for nonzero y.

concepts.title: Directional apparent inertia near singularity
concepts.description: Only the first entry contains1/sin²θ2; the second is constant, illustrating direction-dependent task-space ill-conditioning.

concepts.title: Identify the displayed Jacobian basis
concepts.description: Rotating the base-frame translational velocity into link2-aligned axes gives the displayed matrix; its columns retain length dimensions.

concepts.title: Evaluate the displayed inverse
concepts.description: The lower-triangular inverse has first row(1,0); solving2qdot1+2qdot2=v2 gives the second row(−1,1/2).

concepts.title: Differentiate the displayed Jacobian
concepts.description: The derivatives of the first column are l1cosθ2 qdot2=0 and −l1sinθ2 qdot2=−2; the second column is constant.

concepts.title: Component derivative is not inertial acceleration
concepts.description: The transport theorem adds the basis-rotation term; the slide’s derivative of J_T qdot is a derivative of components unless that term is separately included.
concepts.subtopic: Component derivative is not inertial acceleration

concepts.title: Numerical task inertia
concepts.description: sin²30°=1/4, so m2+m1/sin²θ2=3+2/(1/4)=11 and the second entry remains3.

concepts.title: Evaluate transformed gravity force
concepts.description: The first component is20+30=50 and cos90° makes the second component zero.

concepts.title: Gravity force versus joint gravity torque
concepts.description: Because Gx=J⁻ᵀG, transforming it back gives JᵀGx=G; the force-space vector and joint-effort vector are different objects.
concepts.subtopic: Gravity force versus joint gravity torque

concepts.title: Why the velocity coefficients change
concepts.description: The substitution qddot=J⁻¹(xddot−Jdot qdot) moves a velocity-dependent contribution into the grouped quadratic terms.

concepts.title: Qualify the quoted friction percentage
concepts.description: The page supplies the25% statement without a dataset or operating conditions; the bank can preserve the attribution but cannot establish a universal measured fraction.

concepts.title: Viscous and Coulomb friction
concepts.description: The viscous term is v qdot and the Coulomb term is c sgn(qdot), under the compensating-effort convention.

concepts.title: Compensation and resisting torque have opposite signs
concepts.description: Compensation is2·(−1)+0.5·(−4)=−4; actual friction opposes the negative motion and is therefore+4.
concepts.subtopic: Compensation and resisting torque have opposite signs

concepts.title: Dissipation in the combined friction model
concepts.description: Actual friction power is−c|qdot|−v qdot²; its negative is the nonnegative dissipated power.
concepts.subtopic: Dissipation in the combined friction model

concepts.title: What the simple sign law misses at rest
concepts.description: A single-valued sign-at-zero rule does not model the range of static friction that can balance a load before sliding.
concepts.subtopic: What the simple sign law misses at rest

concepts.title: The reused symbol F
concepts.description: The local definition changes the meaning and coordinate space of F, so its units and role must be read from the equation.

concepts.title: What rigid links omit
concepts.description: Rigid-link dynamics excludes deformation; flexible bending can add resonant behavior beyond that model.

concepts.title: Forward versus inverse dynamics
concepts.description: Forward dynamics determines acceleration from applied effort and the current state; integrating then advances velocity and position.

concepts.title: A coupled forward-dynamics solve
concepts.description: The net right side is(4,4); M⁻¹=(1/3)[[2,−1],[−1,2]], yielding(4/3,4/3).

concepts.title: Complete first-order dynamics
concepts.description: The position derivative is velocity, and the velocity derivative is the forward-dynamics acceleration.

concepts.title: Initial state is not universally at rest
concepts.description: A simulation needs initial position and velocity; zero velocity is one permitted choice.
concepts.subtopic: Initial state is not universally at rest

concepts.title: Distinguish the displayed position update
concepts.description: Plain forward Euler gives q_new=q+qdot Δt; the displayed formula adds the Taylor/constant-acceleration term, while still updating velocity with its first derivative.

concepts.description: The velocity becomes2−0.4=1.6; position becomes1+0.2−0.02=1.18.
